reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports in-situ SiC formation and mechanical strengthening in a different HEA (FeCrNiCu), but provides no data on caloric effects, phase transition tolerance, or the specific (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 system. The key premise that caloric transitions are preserved is entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: In-situ SiC reinforcement can be formed in a high-entropy alloy matrix by adding Si and C during melting
SiC particles improve mechanical properties (hardness, tensile strength) through dislocation strengthening, load bearing, and Orowan mechanisms
The SiC reinforcement does not fundamentally alter the matrix phase structure (FCC) or its intrinsic transitions
The caloric phase transitions in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 are reversible order–disorder transitions that can tolerate a secondary phase
